title: Academic Status by General Weighted Average
breadcrumb: [College Student Handbook > MCM Grading System > Academic Status by GWA]
provenance: The table is a pasted raster image on the PDF page (verify_extraction.py found an extra 397x205 image on page 21 and extract_tables() returned nothing); no parser can read it, so the rows were transcribed by hand from the page image. Boundary note: 3.50 is inclusive at the top of OK (GWA <= 3.50) and exclusive at the bottom of Probationary (3.50 < GWA), so a GWA of exactly 3.50 is OK. Verified against the printed handbook by Mel Macabenta on 2026-07-11. Rows, boundaries and conditions confirmed against printed page 20.
text:
The academic status of a student is determined by his General Weighted Average (GWA) and certain conditions, as follows.
A student with a GWA from 1.00 to 3.50 inclusive has an academic status of OK.
A student with a GWA above 3.50 and up to 4.50 inclusive is placed on Probationary status.
A student is placed Out of the Program under any of the following conditions: (a) a GWA above 4.50 and up to 5.00; (b) two consecutive years classified under Probationary status; or (c) while under Probationary status, the student failed for the third time any course stipulated in the first two years of his curriculum, including PE, NSTP and Values Education.
Original table (Academic Status | Condition/s):
| OK | 1.00 <= GWA <= 3.50 |
| Probationary | 3.50 < GWA <= 4.50 |
| Out of the Program | 4.50 < GWA <= 5.00, or two consecutive years Probationary, or third failure of a first-two-years course while Probationary |
verified_against: Printed page 20, MCM College Student Handbook (2020 edition).
verification_method: Read the printed page side by side with the transcription, row by row.
verification_notes: All three rows confirmed against the printed page. Boundary conditions confirmed as transcribed: 3.50 is inclusive at the top of OK (1.00 <= GWA <= 3.50) and exclusive at the bottom of Probationary (3.50 < GWA <= 4.50). A GWA of exactly 3.50 is OK, not Probationary. The three Out-of-the-Program conditions are disjunctive (any one suffices), not cumulative.

title: Latin Honors GWA Requirements
breadcrumb: [College Student Handbook > MCM Grading System > Latin Honors]
provenance: The table extracts as three columns with the GWA lower bound split from its operator, so a naive row-to-sentence conversion produces wrong boundaries; transcribed by hand. Operator note: Summa's lower bound is inclusive (1.00 <= GWA <= 1.25) while Magna and Cum Laude are exclusive (1.25 < GWA, 1.50 < GWA), so a GWA of exactly 1.25 is Summa Cum Laude and exactly 1.50 is Magna Cum Laude. Verified against the printed handbook by Mel Macabenta on 2026-07-11. The three honors, their GWA ranges and the operator boundaries confirmed against printed page 26.
text:
The following Latin Honors apply to graduating students of baccalaureate programs, based on General Weighted Average (GWA).
A GWA from 1.00 to 1.25 inclusive qualifies for Summa Cum Laude.
A GWA above 1.25 and up to 1.50 inclusive qualifies for Magna Cum Laude.
A GWA above 1.50 and up to 1.75 inclusive qualifies for Cum Laude.
A student with a GWA of exactly 1.25 qualifies for Summa Cum Laude; exactly 1.50 qualifies for Magna Cum Laude; exactly 1.75 qualifies for Cum Laude.
Original table (Latin Honor | GWA):
| SUMMA CUM LAUDE | 1.00 <= GWA <= 1.25 |
| MAGNA CUM LAUDE | 1.25 < GWA <= 1.50 |
| CUM LAUDE | 1.50 < GWA <= 1.75 |
verified_against: Printed page 26, MCM College Student Handbook (2020 edition).
verification_method: Read the printed page side by side with the transcription, row by row.
verification_notes: All three rows confirmed. Operators confirmed as transcribed and they are NOT uniform: Summa's lower bound is inclusive (1.00 <= GWA <= 1.25), while Magna's and Cum Laude's are exclusive (1.25 < GWA <= 1.50; 1.50 < GWA <= 1.75). A student with a GWA of exactly 1.25 qualifies for Summa Cum Laude, not Magna Cum Laude.

title: MCM Grading System: numeric grades, letter grades, and status codes
breadcrumb: [College Student Handbook > MCM Grading System > Grading Scale]
provenance: The grade/descriptor table spans the printed page 16->17 break; the header row appears only on page 16, so the 22 rows on page 17 are unlabelled in isolation. Rows transcribed verbatim from the page image, column labels supplied from page 16. Confirmed against the printed pages on 2026-07-11: (1) The two diploma letter grades appear as -A and -B, minus before the letter, exactly as extracted; this is the handbook's printed form, not an extraction artifact, and both prose and table now render them that way. (2) '2.00 Meritorious' falls between '1.75 Good' and '2.25 Very Satisfactory' -- confirmed as printed; this is the Mapua scale and must not be reordered. (3) Rows B+, B and -B have an empty Baccalaureate cell (preserved as '(blank)'), read as 'not used in baccalaureate programs'; A+, A and -A use '-' for the same meaning. (4) The handbook prints '1.0'; the prose gives both '1.00' and '1.0' so either query form matches, and the preserved table keeps '1.0'. Verified against the printed handbook by Mel Macabenta on 2026-07-11.
text:
In baccalaureate programs, a grade of 1.00 (printed as 1.0 in the handbook) is Excellent, 1.25 is Superior, 1.50 is Very Good, 1.75 is Good, 2.00 is Meritorious, 2.25 is Very Satisfactory, 2.50 is Satisfactory, 2.75 is Fairly Satisfactory, 3.00 is Passed, and 5.00 is Failed; none of these numerical grades apply to diploma programs. The handbook lists no grade between 3.00 and 5.00.
Diploma programs use letter grades instead. As printed in the handbook these are -A (Very Good) and -B (Very Satisfactory), with the minus sign written before the letter; the full set is A+ (Excellent), A (Superior), -A (Very Good), B+ (Good), B (Meritorious), and -B (Very Satisfactory). These letter grades do not apply to baccalaureate programs.
Several marks are shared across both program types: INC means Incomplete, FA means Absent, DRP means Dropped, P means Passed, C means Continuing, F means Failed, AUD means Audit, and NA means Not Applicable. IP indicates a course is In Progress and applies only to baccalaureate programs.

verification_notes:
All 22 rows and the header row confirmed. Three findings, all recorded so they are not 'corrected' later:
(1) THE LETTER GRADES ARE PRINTED -A AND -B, WITH THE MINUS BEFORE THE LETTER. An earlier draft of this chunk asserted A- and B-, inferred from the sequence A+, A, -A, B+, B, -B. That inference was wrong and was reverted on verification against print. The prose and the preserved table both now read -A and -B. Do not change them to A- and B-. The prose names both forms so that a student searching either one still matches.
(2) DO NOT 'CORRECT' THE ORDERING OF THE NUMERIC SCALE. '2.00 Meritorious' falls between '1.75 Good' and '2.25 Very Satisfactory'. This reads as an error and is not one; it is the Mapua scale as printed.
(3) Rows B+, B and -B have an empty Baccalaureate cell in print, where A+, A and -A carry a dash. Both are read here as 'not used in baccalaureate programs'. The preserved table marks the empty cells as (blank) rather than silently filling them with a dash.

text:
Start

1. Complaint Received
The Center for Student Activities and Discipline conducts a preliminary investigation and evaluation to determine prima facie evidence. Complaints must be filed at the Center for Student Activities and Discipline, which holds jurisdiction only in cases where students are respondents.

2. Preliminary Investigation & Evaluation

3. Categorize the Case
Cases are categorized into three types:
a. Cases with an equivalent sanction of suspension for 1-10 days with or without community service
b. Cases with an equivalent sanction of suspension for 11-20 days with or without community service
c. Cases recommended for the Committee on Decorum and Investigation (CDI), upon the discretion of the Center for Student Activities and Discipline based on case complexity

4. Hearing Proper
All cases are heard with strict observance of due process.

5. Decision & Recommendation
After the hearing, a decision or recommendation is formulated for implementation or approval by the concerned office(s).

6. Appeal Process
If No Appeal is made, implementation proceeds after 10 days, leading to the End.

If Yes (An Appeal is Filed):
The case proceeds to the Concerned Office, where a new Decision & Recommendation is formulated, leading to the End.

Appeal Filing Rules:
Appeals for cases with a penalty of suspension under 20% of the prescribed class days for the school year (with or without community service) imposed by the Center for Student Activities and Discipline are filed with the Office of the Principal.

Cases handled by the CDI and those resulting in non-readmission or expulsion are appealed directly to the Office of the Executive Vice President.

text:
PROMOTION AND RETENTION

For Grade 7–10 Learners

If a student achieves a final grade of at least 75 in all learning areas, the decision is promotion to the next grade level.

If a student does not meet expectations in not more than two learning areas, they must pass remedial classes for those failing learning areas to be promoted to the next grade level. Otherwise, the student is retained in the same grade level.

If a student does not meet expectations in three or more learning areas, the decision is retention in the same grade level.

If a student passes all learning areas in Junior High School, they earn a Junior High School Certificate and are promoted to Senior High School.

title: Page 42 (manual correction)
provenance: Manually corrected via the Review tab for page 42.
text:
For Grade 11–12 Learners

When a student achieves final grades of at least 75 in all learning areas in a semester, they can proceed to the next grade level.

When a student does not meet expectations in a prerequisite subject in a learning area, they must pass remedial classes for failed competencies in the subject before being allowed to enroll in the higher level subject.

When a student does not meet expectations in any subject or learning area at the end of the semester, they must pass remedial classes for failed competencies in the subjects or learning areas to be allowed to enroll in the next semester. Otherwise, the learner must retake the subjects failed.

When a student passes all learning areas in Senior High School, they earn a Senior High School Certificate.

Step 1: Start
The process begins when an incident is reported.

Step 2: Complaint Received
Complaints shall be filed at the Prefect of Discipline (POD), which has jurisdiction only in cases where students are the respondents.

Step 3: Preliminary Investigation & Evaluation
The POD conducts a preliminary investigation and evaluation to determine prima facie evidence.

Step 4: Categorize the Case
Cases are categorized into three groups:

Cases with an equivalent sanction of suspension for 1–10 days with or without community service.

Cases with an equivalent sanction of suspension for 22–20 days with or without community service.

Cases recommended for the Committee on Decorum and Investigation (CDI), upon the discretion of the POD based on the complexity of the case.

Step 5: Hearing Proper
All cases will be heard with strict observance of due process.

Step 6: Decision & Recommendation
After hearing the case, a decision or recommendation will be formulated for implementation and approval by the concerned office or offices.

Step 7: Appeal Decision

If Appealed (Yes): The case is routed to the Concerned Office. Appeals for cases with an equivalent penalty of suspension of less than 20% of the prescribed class days for the school year (with or without community service) imposed by the POD shall be filed with the Office of the Principal. Cases handled by the CDI and those with an equivalent sanction of non-readmission and/or expulsion shall be filed with the Office of Executive Vice President. The office then formulates a final Decision & Recommendation.

If Not Appealed (No): Implementation takes effect after 10 days, as the decision becomes final and executory after 10 days.

Step 8: End
The process concludes.

title: OTHER SECURITY MEASURES:
provenance: Manually corrected via Page Explorer for page 11.
text:
The Learners' IDs are embedded with an RFID system that they must TAP- IN and TAP-OUT at the school's entry points kiosks. This enables the school's system to know when a student has entered the campus, which building they enter, and at what time they entered. The system also tracks the learners' TAP-OUT, signifying that the student has left the building.
Security checkpoints are in place at the entry points to the High School Department.
Security personnel at these checkpoints shall monitor the entry and exit of High School learners. High School learners may be prevented from exiting, espec ially during class hours. Learners may obtain special exit passes from the Principal's Office if they will need to exit the Mapúa MCM campus before the end of their scheduled classes. Security personnel at these checkpoints shall also monitor the entry of College students into the High School department area. College students who will need to enter the High School department area will have to secure special entry passes from their respective deans or program chairs, then noted by the High School Administrative Officer or Principal. High School learners, although not yet of legal age, are assumed to be capable of making good decisions for their own safety and well-being. MAPÚA MCM-HS' Security personnel will therefore be limited to the following guidelines for HS Learners on leaving the campus:
High School Learners who are not riding the Mapúa MCM-accredited school buses will not be prevented from leaving the campus after class hours.
Those taking the public transportation, fetched by their own vehicles by parents or guardians, or carpooling with other learners, are presumed to be going home immediately after classes when they tap out of an Mapúa MCM entry/exit kiosk. If not, they are presumed to have informed their parents or guardians of their after-school activities and destination before heading home. Mapúa MCM cannot be held liable for the learners who have left Mapúa MCM's jurisdiction.
Mapúa MCM Security personnel, however, are trained and instructed to take note of any unusual scenarios or student behaviors, and shall therefore report these to school administrators and/or prevent High School learners from leaving the campus (e.g. talks of going to some places of ill-repute, planning an impromptu overnight outings, suspicious-looking vehicles and personnel fetching learners).
Should some parents want their child to be prevented from leaving the campus unless fetched by a specific person and/or vehicle, they will have to put this request into writing, addressed to the Principal.
If the learners have finished their classes and are intending to stay within the campus, they may be allowed to stay in the following areas in the Mapúa MCM campus:
Soccer Field 
Library
Covered Court 
Designated Student Lounges
Cafeteria

1. Any act of Dishonesty such as but not limited to the following:

1.1 Cheating in examinations, unauthorized possession/use of notes or any materials relevant to the examination during the exam:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) AND Zero in graded activity.
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) AND Zero in graded activity.

4th Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) AND Zero in graded activity.
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) AND Zero in graded activity.
3rd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) AND Failure in the Subject.
4th Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

1.3 Communicating (through any medium) with another student/any other person (inside or outside examination room) during examination, without permission from the professor or proctor:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) AND Zero in graded activity.

1.4 Plagiarism, or submitting another person's work as one's own:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Academic Sanctions OR Dismissal from the Institute.

1.5 Massive, pre-meditated, organized cheating including but not limited to major exams:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Academic Sanctions OR Dismissal from the Institute.

1.6 Other forms of cheating during examination, in passing of homework or assigned projects or any other academic work:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) AND Zero in graded activity.
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Academic Sanctions.
3rd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

1.7 Falsification of documents, forgery and or any similar acts of alteration but not limited to:

1.7.1 Alteration or misuse of school documents in connection with official matters:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Academic Sanctions OR Dismissal from the Institute.

1.7.2 Alteration or misuse of school records or credentials:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Academic Sanctions OR Dismissal from the Institute.

1.7.3 Submission of false or fraudulent information and/or documents to the Institute in connection with official matters:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Academic Sanctions OR Dismissal from the Institute.

1.7.4 Publication or dissemination of false information about the school administration, its officials, faculty members, or learners:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute OR Expulsion.

1.7.5. Forging of security stamp to gain entry to the institute:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) OR Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

1.8 Lending or borrowing of school ID, official receipt, certificate of matriculation, or other official documents and/or presenting another person's documents as one's own; tampering of school ID and into using it to gain entry the Institute:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) OR Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

2. Accumulation of any four (4) minor offenses of any nature within one (1) quarter of the school year:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
3rd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

3. Physical injury/assault upon any member of the faculty, administration, staff; or any student, personnel, or visitor of the Institute:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Academic Sanctions OR Dismissal from the Institute OR Expulsion.

4. Any acts of threat either physical or by means of any medium of communications including but not limited to: oral, through social media, and using any electronic gadgets against any school officials, faculty member, employee, student and or any visitor of the Institute:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) OR Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Academic Sanctions OR Dismissal from the Institute OR Expulsion.

5. Discourtesy in any form (physical/ oral, written) by means of any medium of communication, such as, but not limited to:

5.1. Bullying, defamation, inciting to fight, and/or any abusive behavior committed against any student:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) OR Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

5.2. Disrespect toward any faculty member, or any official of the Institute or his authorized representative:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) OR Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

5.3. Failure to comply with the deadline given/ set to complete the given disciplinary sanction and/or to submit an explanation letter for commission of any of the minor offense; unless justified:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
3rd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

6. Any other conduct which threatens, endangers, or adversely affects the health or safety of any person inside MAPÚA MCM premises:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) OR Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

7. Illegal possession of deadly weapon of any kind and or use of explosives, incendiary devices, and/or any other similar devices:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

8. Forcible entry to the campus:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

9. Unauthorized use of MAPÚA MCM facilities and services but not limited to:

9.1. Unauthorized use of rooms:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
3rd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

9.2. Tampering with or misuse of computer applications, software programs, and other IT systems of the Institute, whether or not for personal advantage, including but not limited to manipulating enrolment procedures and requirements, grades, class schedules, tuition and matriculation, and student records, or any willful or negligent act resulting in computer security breach:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) OR Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

10. Any form of bribery (attempted or consummated) of any faculty member or personnel of the Institute:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

11. Stealing, attempting and/or facilitating to steal:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) OR Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

12. Vandalism, or the willful or negligent destruction of any property of the Institute which includes, but is not limited to such acts as tearing off or defacing any library book, magazine or periodical; writing, drawing, or posting unauthorized notices on walls or pieces of furniture, breakage of glass windows, showcases, cabinet doors, electrical and mechanical devices or contrivances; unauthorized removal of official notices and posters from bulletin boards and other similar acts, or causing other damage to any property of the Institute:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) OR Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

13. Unauthorized/misuse of emergency switch such as but not limited to fire alarms, activation of water sprinklers and the likes:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service) OR Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).

14. Hazing or the infliction of any physical or mental harm or ordeal on any person, which injures, degrades, or disgraces or that tends to injure, degrade, or disgrace any fellow student or any person in the Institute:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

15. Forming, recruiting, and/or joining any surreptitious or clandestine organization like fraternities and sororities, or other associations formed for illegal, immoral, unethical purposes, or those not officially recognized by the Office of Student Activities or not listed in the official list of organizations:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

17. Unauthorized possession and/or drinking of alcoholic beverages within the premises of the Institute whether or not in connection with an official school activity approved by the Office of Student Activities; drinking outside the premises of the Institute in connection with an official school activity approved by the Office of the Student Activities; or entering the campus under the influence of alcohol:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

18. Public display of Affection (PDA), which offends or tends to offend the sensibilities of the Academic Community or inappropriate intimate physical contact including, but not limited to: intimate touching, kissing, hugging, lying / leaning on another person, etc. within the school premises or at any school-sponsored activity:
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
3rd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

19. Engaging in lewd, obscene, or immoral conduct within the campus premises:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

20. Engaging in any form of gambling within the premises of the Institute:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
3rd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

21. Smoking at any time within the school premises:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
3rd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

22. All forms of student protests whose distinctive characteristics are physical force, violence, threat and intimidation:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

23. Posting and/or distributing literature, pamphlets, pictures, news items or any announcement whatsoever without any written permit from the Office of the Student Activities:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
3rd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

24. Organizing, participating in and/or supporting any activity inside or outside the school campus, without approval from the Office of Student Activities or appropriate school authorities:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
3rd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

25. Instigating or leading an illegal strike or similar activities resulting in disruption or stoppage of classes:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Academic Sanctions OR Dismissal from the Institute.

26. Unauthorized collection or exaction of money, checks, or other instruments of monetary equivalent from any student, faculty member, or employee, whether or not in connection with matters pertaining to the Institute:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

27. Embezzlement of funds of a student organization or student council:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

28. Willful failure to comply with instruction (either oral or a written), summons and/or notices given/issued for purposes of investigation conducted in connection with discipline related offenses, or any matters related/in connection to the official function of the Institute in accordance with law of the land:
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
3rd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

29. Perjury, lying or giving false statements in any administrative proceeding and/or presenting false documents to mislead an investigation during the administrative proceedings:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

30. Violation of any penal statute or of rules and regulations promulgated by the Department of Education, of the policies and regulations of MAPÚA MCM or of any valid order by proper authorities:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

31. Habitual tardiness (6 or more repeated tardiness spread through the semester):
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).

32. Discourtesy or disrespect to faculty members, employees, learners and visitors:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

33. Misbehavior during school programs, activities and events:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
3rd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

34. Disrespect for national and MAPÚA MCM symbols:
1st Offense: Suspension for 1-10 days (with/without community service).
2nd Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service).
3rd Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

35. Conviction before any court for a criminal offense involving moral turpitude against persons or property other than through reckless imprudence:
1st Offense: Dismissal from the Institute.

36. Any other acts that compromise the name and reputation of MAPÚA MCM as a premier educational institution:
1st Offense: Suspension for 11-20 days (with/without community service) OR Dismissal from the Institute.

Additional Policy Notes:

Deadline of the completion of the community service given as sanction both for minor and major infractions to a student shall be determined by the Center for Student Activities and Discipline in consideration of the academic schedule and activities of the student.

Student liability shall NOT be confined to the enumeration because some may be generally worded to encompass related wrong doings.

In order for the learners to understand the gravity of their misdemeanor, the CSAD Coordinator can require them to undergo counseling, whose frequency and duration shall be fixed according to the discretion of the Head of the Center for Guidance and Counseling.

The Institute reserves the right to impose other sanctions other than those stipulated in this handbook provided that it is in accordance with the law.
